newsitem.title: USA: Universal earnings up as tobacco leaf volumes rise.
newsitem.headline: Universal earnings up as tobacco leaf volumes rise.

text.p: Universal Corp., whose businesses include tobacco and lumber, said Thursday its second quarter earnings rose amid better tobaccco leaf volumes.
Net income in the second quarter ended Dec. 31, rose to $31.4 million, or 90 cents per share, from $27.4 million, or 78 cents a share, a year earlier.
Revenues were $1.3 billion vs. $1 billion a year earlier.

Tobacco earnings grew moderately in the quarter and remained sharply higher for the year reflecting larger leaf volumes purchased and processed and a return to better operating margins, Chairman Henry Harrell said in a statement.
Non-tobacco operations reported significant growth in the second quarter led by a strong performance in the lumber and building products area, Universal said.
For the six months, net income was $51.4 million, $1.47 a share, compared with $37.6 million, or $1.07 a share, in fiscal year 1996. Revenues were $2.2 billion, up from $1.9 billion a year earlier.
Universal stock was up 87.5 cents to $31.75 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
